text:
maya: Promotion stuck on canary -> deploy-bot returned manifest attach error. Holding cut until artifact is fixed.

deploy-bot: ERROR attaching blob: manifest missing or TTL expired (HTTP 409)
  request id: rq_8f3a2
  command: promote --env=canary --artifact=redwood-service:2026-03-01

alex: any quick repro logs? is this the registry or our upload job failing?

maya: digging. CI shows the artifact upload succeeded, but the registry garbage-collected manifest after TTL renewal failed. logs:
```
2026-03-01T12:05:23Z upload: manifest pushed sha256:abcd1234
2026-03-01T12:07:01Z registry: manifest ttl refresh failed status=500 err="db timeout"
2026-03-01T12:09:10Z promote: attach attempt -> 409 manifest missing
```

tom: hmm ok. Two options: 1) re-publish the manifest (repush same image digest) and re-run promote, or 2) pin release to previous good digest and roll forward later.

sei: +1 for republish if we can guarantee same digest and immutability. If repush not possible quickly, we should rollback canary to previous sha to avoid blocking the release window.

ops-oncall: ETA to republish? who has access to the registry keys for a direct manifest write?

jordan: I can run a republish job from the build artifacts. steps: fetch blob by digest, push manifest referencing existing blob. I need a greenlight and the registry creds (CI service account).

maya: jordan go for it. tagging ops-oncall for creds: @ops-oncall can you scope a short-lived token for ci-service-account that allows manifest:write on artifacts/redwood-service? We want to avoid full write perms.

ops-oncall: granting token now, expires in 30m. token id: tok_promote_03. Be careful, audit will flag direct writes.

jordan: running republish now. command:
```
# fetch blobs
registry-cli pull --digest sha256:abcd1234 --out /tmp/blobs
# push manifest referencing blobs
registry-cli push-manifest --name redwood-service --digest sha256:abcd1234 --manifest /tmp/blobs/manifest.json --token tok_promote_03
```

ci-bot: pipeline 2245 rerun requested by jordan (artifact re-publish). status: queued.

deploy-bot: Promotion retry queued: promote --env=canary --artifact=redwood-service:2026-03-01 (attempt 2)

alex: if republish succeeds we should still pin the release notes and CI tag to the digest, not the mutable tag. otherwise we'll get another surprise.

maya: agreed. once canary is up we'll pin release to digest and add a note in the changelog: "hotfix: re-published manifest after registry TTL failure; pinned to sha256:abcd1234". Also schedule a postmortem with registry team.

jordan: republish succeeded, registry now returns manifest present. logs:
```
2026-03-01T12:18:02Z manifest write ok sha256:abcd1234
2026-03-01T12:18:10Z promote attach ok
```

deploy-bot: Promotion succeeded -> canary deployed (release id: r-2026-03-01-canary).

sei: canary health checks passing 3/3. holding other rollouts for 15m for observation.

maya: moving forward: 1) pin release to digest sha256:abcd1234 in release notes and CI metadata, 2) add registry TTL refresh alert to SLO playbook, 3) schedule 1-hour postmortem with registry and infra tomorrow 10am.

tom: for immediate mitigation I'd like a script to re-run manifest refresh on new uploads until we fix the TTL bug. I'll open a quick PR with that helper.

ops-oncall: noted. audit entry created for tok_promote_03 and manifest write.

alex: also update runbook to prefer digest pinning for releases and avoid promoting mutable tags directly. small change but will save pain.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll draft the release note blurb now and tag security/legal if needed for auditing. If any issues pop in the next 15m we rollback, but current canary looks good. :thumbsup:

jordan: leaving logs and exact commands in the artifacts channel.

ci-bot: pipeline 2245 completed: success.

maya: closing thread, will follow up with PM and registry team on postmortem invite.
